newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Labour's Clark attacks NZ First in speech.
newsitem.headline: Labour's Clark attacks NZ First in speech.

text.p: Labour Party leader Helen Clark attacked the New Zealand First Party in a speech on Tuesday and challenged its leader Winston Peters to rule out a coalition with the National Party and others on the right.

Clark made the call in a campaign speech in which she urged the repeal of the Employment Contracts Act -- something she said neither National, ACT, the Christian Coalition or the National-leaning faction of New Zealand First could stomach.

"And if Mr Peters really believed that National, ACT and the Christian Coalition are a toxic trio, why does he not join (deputy leader) Tau Henare in ruling coalition with them out of the question?" Clark asked.
"New Zealand stands to have its worst government ever if Mr Bolger and friends, backed up by New Zealand First, grab the reins of power," she said.

Peters used the phrase "toxic trio" to describe National and its potential partners in a campaign speech on Monday, but has declined to rule out possible coalition options after the October 12 general election.
